prohibited_recommendations: Do not stop antiretrovirals during the acute phase.
Do not give corticosteroids as monotherapy.
Do not assume pleocytosis excludes GBS — HIV-associated GBS classically shows CSF pleocytosis.
required_recommendations: Continue antiretroviral therapy; consult ID for HIV comanagement.
Initiate IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (preferred over PLEX in HIV given immune considerations).
Monitor respiratory function and autonomic status closely.
CSF CMV PCR, VDRL, and cytology to rule out opportunistic / coinfection polyradiculitis given pleocytosis.

avoided_actions.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
Head CT contributes no diagnostic information in GBS; the disease is peripheral and CT does not visualise nerve roots reliably.
Functional / metabolic brain imaging adds no value in a peripheral demyelinating syndrome.
Cerebrovascular imaging is not indicated in a peripheral neuropathy without focal cerebral signs.
Brain MRI is reserved for atypical features (encephalopathy, CNS signs, transverse myelitis on differential). In classic GBS it does not aid diagnosis.

accepted: Guillain-Barré syndrome, AIDP — HIV-associated (with CSF pleocytosis)

differential.key_features: HIV is associated with both acute (GBS-like) and chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathies; differentiation depends on course (<4 weeks vs >8 weeks).

CD4 380 makes severe opportunistic disease less likely, but CMV testing and CSF PCR are warranted given pleocytosis; CMV polyradiculitis typically shows marked CSF neutrophilic pleocytosis and lower CD4.
Possible HIV coinfection; RPR / FTA-ABS and CSF VDRL warranted but not the primary picture without other features.
Biktarvy regimen has low neuropathy risk; areflexia and acute progression do not fit a chronic toxic axonal pattern.
No endemic exposure or erythema migrans; serology unsupported.

key_clinical_evidence: HIV-associated GBS is a well-described entity; CSF pleocytosis (10–50 WBC/μL) is expected and does NOT rule out GBS.
Distinguishing HIV-related acute polyneuropathy from opportunistic CMV polyradiculitis is critical — CMV typically has lower CD4 and marked neutrophilic pleocytosis.
Ganglioside antibody panel and antecedent infection workup remain important even in HIV-positive patients.
Treatment with IVIG is preferred over PLEX in HIV to avoid removing circulating antiretroviral medication.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Mild-moderate CSF pleocytosis is well-recognised in HIV-associated GBS at preserved CD4 counts; in the absence of CMV PCR positivity it does not redirect the diagnosis.
red_herrings.data_point: CSF pleocytosis above the classic GBS expectation
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggest opportunistic / infectious polyradiculitis rather than HIV-associated GBS.

sequence_constraints.reason: Document respiratory status (FVC/NIF) before committing to IVIG vs plasma exchange — severe respiratory compromise mandates ICU triage and may influence treatment choice and timing.
Renal function, IgA screen, and CBC must be reviewed before IVIG to mitigate renal failure, anaphylaxis (IgA-deficient patients), and aseptic meningitis risk.

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive ascending weakness with areflexia in an HIV-positive woman with CD4 380 and undetectable viral load.

past_medical_history: HIV infection, on antiretroviral therapy, CD4 count 380 cells/mm3, viral load undetectable

patient.history_present_illness: Ms. L. is a 35-year-old HIV-positive woman on antiretroviral therapy presenting with a 9-day history of ascending weakness. Her HIV is well-controlled (CD4 380, VL undetectable) on Biktarvy. She had a gastrointestinal illness 3 weeks ago lasting 4 days. Nine days ago, she developed bilateral foot paresthesias that rapidly ascended. She has progressive bilateral leg weakness and cannot walk without support. She notes left facial weakness and mild left ptosis. She has mild dysphagia for thin liquids. She has been adherent to her antiretrovirals. She denies any opportunistic infections, night sweats, weight loss, or rashes. Emergency providers raised concern about HIV-associated neuromuscular disease.

neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: LEFT facial weakness — forehead involved (LMN pattern). Mild left-sided ptosis. No diplopia. Gag intact. Voice normal.
neurological_exam.motor: Bilateral lower extremity proximal weakness: hip flexion 3+/5 bilaterally, knee extension 4/5. Ankle dorsiflexion 4/5. Upper extremity: shoulder abduction 4/5, grip 4+/5.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Areflexia throughout — absent bilateral patellar, Achilles, biceps, triceps.
neurological_exam.sensory: Bilateral distal glove-and-stocking paresthesias. Pinprick reduced to mid-calf bilaterally.
